title: Self-WSP: Can Language Models Improve Themselves Through Weight-Space Programming?
read_level: full main text, limitations and ethics; appendices A-D skimmed (Table 1 numbers not fully extractable from PDF text)
why_wsp: Qwen3.5-0.8B reads statistics/values of its own weights, proposes grammar-constrained JSON edits (scale, shift, zero, etc.), and the kept edited weights become both solver and next editor, with an outer loop accepting edits that improve practice-question accuracy.
editor: Qwen3.5-0.8B (itself; thinking off as editor); comparisons to GPT-6 Astra edits from Takehi et al. 2026 and to a random sampler
target: Qwen3.5-0.8B (24 layers, catalog of 318 editable tensors)
interface: direct values (grammar-constrained JSON edits over blocks: zero, scale, add, fill, redraw, remove direction, NumPy expression)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (rounds with fixed edit budgets; keep edit if practice-batch gains; validation-based selection of runs)
self_editing: yes; the same model is editor and solver and each kept edit changes both roles (a frozen-editor control is also run)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "The 24.2% MATH500 model differs from the original model in only 16 numbers"; "No selected model changes more than 0.2% of its weights" (Sec. 3)

headline_results.quote: Self-edits can raise GSM8K accuracy from 11.8% to 62.2% and MATH500 accuracy from 7.0% to 32.2%, sometimes by changing only 16 parameters
Of the 24 selected models in Table 1, 22 are significantly better than the original model
they gain on average 24.7 points on GSM8K and 7.7 points on MATH500, far less than the selected models
Its best model scores 32.8% against 31.9% for self-editing

headline_results.claim: Random search fails on MATH500 with same budget
headline_results.quote: With the same budget, random search finds no improvement, while selfediting reaches 17.3%.
Of the 11,580 proposals the editor made, 69% are invalid even though the grammar guarantees their format.
headline_results.where: Sec. 3 (also: "Only 12% of the valid edits are kept")

headline_results.quote: GPT-6's best edit, which reaches 66.9% in our evaluation
Across all 12 eight-round runs on MATH, kept edits leave validation accuracy unchanged on average.

baselines_and_controls: Unedited original model (same hardware and sampling seeds); random search with same and ~1.7-2x budget; 352 single random edits per dataset with sampling-noise band; frozen editor (original weights) control; GPT-6 Astra's two published edits re-evaluated; pre-designated spot-check runs.
runs_and_variance: 12 or 24 runs per setting; Top-3 selected per setting evaluated once on test sets; six spot-check runs per dataset under ordered interface; sampling-noise range from re-answering with other seeds (5th-95th percentile band).
robustness_of_edits: not tested (no fine-tuning/quantization/distribution-shift tests); notes "more than 40% of the rounds that keep an edit lower validation accuracy" under shuffled interface
verification: statistical only (significance vs original model; noise band); no formal verification
memorization_vs_reasoning: Evidence of pattern-copying: "Between 9% and 28% of the values in valid edits equal a statistic the editor has just read"; edit location follows catalog order ("layer 0 receives 62%" under ordered interface); explanations "often hallucinated".
limitations_stated: Single small model on two math benchmarks; main weakness (repetitive thinking) unusually easy to repair; outer loop uses reference answers so improvement is supervised; ordered interface designed after seeing shuffled results; no random search under ordered interface; GPT-6 comparison only indicative.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026, Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog)
Fan et al. 2026, Language models can rewrite their own weights
notes_for_survey: Direct B6 self-editing study with strong controls (random search, single random edits, frozen editor, spot-check runs). Gains are attributed mainly to the outer selection loop and to breaking repetitive thinking (original model fails to finish ~90% of questions within 32k tokens); editor understanding of its edits is weak.
